q: What's the safest way to test that before committing?
answer:
Run a staged A/B test on Meta by campaign: cut spend in a controlled subset of campaigns (or ad sets) and measure the actual sales/profit impact before you change account-level budgets. This limits downside while giving a clean signal about responsiveness.

How to run it (safe, low-risk steps)
- Pick the test window and sample: 14 days is a good balance (gives enough conversions). Compare it with the immediately preceding 14-day window (same weekdays) so seasonality is matched.
- Test design (two patterns; pick one):
  - Holdout campaigns: keep a set of stable campaigns at current spend (control) and reduce spend by 30% in a matched set of similar campaigns (treatment). Match by historical spend, ROAS and audience. This isolates the effect of spend changes.
  - Geo / audience split: run the 30% cut in one geography or audience segment and keep the other as control (useful when campaigns target many regions).
- Metrics to watch (by order date basis):
  - Primary: Net sales (P&L basis) (P&L net sales) and net profit (order-date net profit) — the business outcome.
  - Secondary: orders, AOV, return rate / cancelled orders, and ad spend (P&L: Ad spend (P&L basis)). Watch conversion rate (sessions → orders) if you can align it.
  - Timing: check early signals (3–4 days) but make decisions only after the full 14-day window.
- Analysis approach:
  - Compare absolute net profit and net sales (not ratios) between treatment and control for the test window vs their previous windows; use percent change and contribution to overall profit.
  - Flag campaign-level winners/losers by whether the treatment lost more profit than the ad spend saved.
  - Watch for delayed effects (higher returns or cancellations in subsequent days); extend observation for returns if needed.
- Practical safeguards:
  - Don’t cut all spend in any campaign; phase the reduction (start with a smaller initial cut, then move to 30%) to reduce shock and get early signals.
  - Limit the test to campaigns that historically drove measurable sales (enough orders) — avoid experimenting on very low-volume campaigns where results are “early signals.”
  - Keep creatives, landing pages and bids constant during the test; only change budget to isolate spend effect.
  - Pre-register the decision rule: e.g., if net profit across treatment is better by at least the saved spend after 14 days, roll the cut wider; if net sales fall beyond the breakeven threshold, revert.

Worth checking: run the test by campaign on Meta with ad spend (P&L), net sales (P&L basis) and net profit; audit campaign-level results for “spend that bought nothing” before scaling the cut.
